subject: Order Form - COI naming + additional insured language clarification
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@bluehorizon.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@bluehorizon.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on insurance naming & COI for Order Form

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for sending over the latest order form redline (attached). Our procurement/legal team had two quick questions on the insurance section before we sign: 

1) Additional insured: your redline asks that Blue Horizon be added as an Additional Insured on Redwood's auto and general liability policies. Can you confirm the exact wording you need on the endorsement? Our broker prefers to use a standard endorsement but wants to make sure it satisfies your procurement team.

2) Certificate of Insurance (COI): do you require any particular proof beyond a COI (e.g., endorsement copies naming Blue Horizon, carrier contact, policy number redaction rules)? We can provide a COI and an endorsement PDF, but want to avoid unnecessary back-and-forth.

I've attached our redline to reference the section (BlueHorizon_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick call if easier. 

Regards,

Sara Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Blue Horizon AI
[Attachment: BlueHorizon_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@bluehorizon.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on insurance naming & COI for Order Form

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the redline. Looping in Neha from Legal and Rishi from Sales so we can give you a short, binding answer. 

Quick summary: we typically require
- Commercial General Liability (CGL) w/ limits of $2M aggregate and $1M per occurrence
- Auto Liability: $1M combined single limit
- Waiver of subrogation in favor of customer is negotiable and varies by contract tier

For the Additional Insured endorsement we ask for the following naming language (preferred):
"Blue Horizon AI, its officers, directors, employees and agents are named as Additional Insured, but only with respect to liability arising out of Redwood Inference's performance under the Agreement."

Neha — can you confirm whether that preferred phrasing is acceptable and whether an ACORD COI plus an endorsement PDF satisfies proof requirements, or whether Blue Horizon needs the carrier to sign anything else?

Sara — if your broker can provide the ACORD 25 COI referencing the policy number (policy number may be partially redacted), and a scanned PDF of the endorsement with the naming above, that will generally be fine for our procurement intake. If there are specific carrier restrictions we should know about, flag them and we can escalate.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_COI_Sample.pdf (PDF stub)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@bluehorizon.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on insurance naming & COI for Order Form

Hi Sara and team — quick legal guidance from our side.

1) Additional Insured wording: the phrasing Tessa proposed is acceptable. If your broker uses an industry-standard CG 20 10 (or CG 20 26) endorsement that names Blue Horizon AI in the same scope (limited to Redwood's operations under the Agreement), that will work. Please ensure the endorsement includes the effective dates that match the term of the Order Form.

2) COI + endorsement proof: an ACORD 25 COI together with a scanned endorsement PDF is acceptable for onboarding. We do request that the endorsement explicitly list Blue Horizon AI (no abbreviations) and include the endorsement form number if available. Partial redaction of policy numbers is fine; carrier and limits must be visible.

3) Auto Liability: please confirm the insured's name on the auto policy matches the legal entity executing the Redwood Order Form. If vehicles are hired/leased by another entity, we may need confirmation or an alternate endorsement.

4) Timing: procurement typically needs the COI + endorsement delivered prior to countersignature or concurrently with countersignature. If Blue Horizon needs countersigned docs first, let us know and we can work with Sales for an accommodation.

I have attached a sample COI (Redwood_COI_Sample.pdf) and a short suggested amendment you can drop into the Order Form if helpful (OrderForm_amendment_0819.docx).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_amendment_0819.docx (DOCX)]
